title: Expected scalar Taylor error
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ satisfy the fourth-order invariance moment conditions: it has finite fourth absolute moment, and its first, second, and third moments are $0,1,0$, respectively, with fourth moment at most $9$. Let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be four times continuously differentiable, and suppose $C\ge0$ and $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Then for all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, \[\left|\int_\Omega\psi(a+bX(\omega))\,d\mu(\omega)-\left(\psi(a)+\frac{\psi''(a)}2b^2\right)\right|\le\frac{3C}{8}b^4.\]
hypotheses_covered: $X$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions, including finite fourth absolute moment, moments $0,1,0$ of orders one through three, and fourth moment at most $9$
replaced: Let $X$ be a real input on a probability space, measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. Let $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be $C^4$ and let $C\ge0$ satisfy $|\psi^{(4)}(t)|\le C$ for all real $t$. For all real $a,b$, $|\mathbb E\psi(a+bX)-\psi(a)-\tfrac12\psi^{(2)}(a)b^2|\le(3C/8)b^4$.
